calibration.description: Real OpenCV-format calibration from a real camera (not synthetic). Computed by the Camera Calibration Toolbox for MATLAB (Bouguet/Caltech) from 3 real photographs of a planar checkerboard, taken 2012-05-24 with a Fujifilm FinePix 6900 Zoom (verified via EXIF metadata on the source images: model=FinePix6900ZOOM, native resolution 2048x1536). Source: https://johnloomis.org/ece564/notes/CameraCalibration/2012_0524/example_calib.html (archived reproduction of a standard Bouguet toolbox worked example; raw images downloaded and inspected directly to confirm camera model and native pixel resolution).
calibration.k3_note: 6th-order radial term not estimated in the source calibration run (disabled/left at 0), per the source page. Not a fabricated value.

sensor_physical_mm.note: 1/1.7-inch optical format, the documented CCD type of the Fujifilm FinePix 6900 Zoom (Super CCD, 1/1.7"). This is the standard published physical size for this sensor format, not a value read off the calibration itself (OpenCV calibration alone yields focal length only in pixel units and does not determine physical sensor size).

calibration.aspect_ratio_note: width/pixel_width == height/pixel_height exactly (7.60/2048 == 5.70/1536), but fx != fy in the real calibration, so a single scalar F cannot exactly satisfy both axes simultaneously (see single_focal_length_compatibility in PrincipalPointConversion.lean). F is derived from the x-axis (F=(w/ws)*fx), matching hF_eq in Pipeline/PixelIff.lean; the y-axis check in run.py is informational only for this reason, not a pass/fail signal for the F-vs-F^2 question.
